chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about buying gold containing silver with gold. He said, 'It is not valid except with dinars and dirhams.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for validly selling gold containing silver for pure gold in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism for avoiding *riba al-fadl* in mixed-metal transactions by mandating the use of standard pure coins (dinars and dirhams) as the unit of measure. This ruling ensures that when gold containing silver impurities is exchanged for pure gold, the transaction is treated as a sale of the pure component against its equivalent, thereby preserving the integrity of the 'same kind, equal measure' principle. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise measurement in commodity exchanges to prevent hidden usury.
